column1: # Old Norse for the "Write in ..." tool (scribe.js); built into scribe-langs.js by scripts/make-scribe.ps1.
# The Younger Futhark: 16 runes for many sounds (d and t, g and k, e and i, o, u, v, w and y share runes), in its two
# forms, the long-branch runes of the Danish stones and the short-twig runes of Sweden and Norway. A doubled letter is
# written once, as on the stones. Values follow the usual transliteration of runic inscriptions (Rundata).

column4: Old Norse was carved in runes, the Younger Futhark of sixteen letters, on stones, wood and bone; from the 11th and 12th centuries it was also written in the Latin alphabet.

column2: The long-branch runes (“Danish” runes) of the Viking Age, carved on the great stones of Denmark such as Harald Bluetooth’s at Jelling, around 965.

Type Old Norse or any name: the sixteen runes stand for more sounds than they have letters, so d is written as t, g as k, e as i, and o, v, w and y as u, as the carvers did. A doubled letter is written once. ʀ (on its key) is the r that came from an older z. Spaces become the small dot between words.

column2: The short-twig runes (“Swedish-Norwegian” runes), quicker to cut, used in Sweden and Norway from the 9th century, as on the Rök stone.
The same sixteen runes in their shorter forms. Type as for the long-branch runes: d is written as t, g as k, e as i, o, v, w and y as u; a doubled letter is written once.
